title: Meeting Oscar Pettiford at the White Rose Bar
summary: Stewart met Pettiford on the Street, the two hung out at the White Rose, and he judges Pettiford very good but not quite Blanton.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Now, when you met -- you met Pettiford on 52nd Street. Did you meet him like after he played or after you played or did you meet him in a social setting?

I met him -- he was playing in a little spot down the street. He was playing with another group, and I met a lot of the fellows on the Street, you know. And we -- Oscar and I, we became very friendly, and we used to meet whenever we can -- we could, rather -- around the corner at our favorite hangout. The White Rose Bar, you know, a lot of musicians used to hang out there, and it was our meeting place, you know, where we used to get together, have a drink or two and chat and talk about our music and where we'd been between sets.
And the street was really quite a place.
What kind of -- how did Pettiford strike you as a bassist at that time?
Oh, he was good, a good bassist. In fact, I think he worked with Ellington for a while there too.
Yeah. And when he was with Ellington, I think, they had two basses at one time.
Did he strike you as being as good a bassist as Blanton was?
Well, no, not quite, although he was very good. And some of the things he did was very impressive.
Oh, some of the fast numbers that he used to play. I can't quite remember some of them.
I don't mean necessarily the tunes, but what was it that you were impressed by?
Well, he handled that bass very well. Yes. Fast too.
Fast. He had a big sound?
Big sound, yeah. Somewhat like Jimmy Blanton.
